name: Dokusha moderu (reader model)

card.summary: Amateur readers picked by Japanese fashion magazines to model, whose hair, makeup and outfits set accessible, copyable trends.

quick.overview:
A dokusha moderu, or dokumo, is an amateur model drawn from a magazine's readership who poses in its pages while keeping an ordinary job or studies. Because they look like the readers, their hair, makeup and clothing are seen as achievable.

Many are found by street snaps, where editors photograph passersby, or by applications at the back of the magazine. Some have started trends, such as the aomoji-kei look in Harajuku.
quick.how: Readers copy the styles, makeup demonstrations and makeup books published by dokumo, and attend fan events. Some dokumo go on to act, sing or launch brands.
quick.risks: No health risks are specific to the role. Commentary questions whether dokumo are comparable to contracted professional models.

lead: Dokusha moderu, literally reader models, are amateur fashion models drawn from a magazine's readers who appear alongside regular work or study.[1][2] They are usually found through street snaps or through an application form in the magazine, and they demonstrate outfits and makeup.[1]

For people working on their appearance, dokumo offer reference looks they feel they can copy. Rina Tanaka, Fumiko Aoyagi, Ayumi Seto and Natsume Mito helped start the aomoji-kei style in Harajuku, and Mito's short high bangs became a signature.[1]
The magazine Popteen, which began in 1980 and ended in February 2023, was known for letting readers become models and for covering gyaru fashion.[3]

Readers copy hairstyles, makeup and outfits
angle.text: Dokumo model styles viewed as attainable by ordinary readers, who adopt their hair, makeup and clothing. Makeup books by dokumo sell widely.

paras: Dokusha means reader. Dokumo are magazine readers who model, often in small spreads, and who now work on television, online media and beyond.[1] Their appeal is accessibility: they often keep ordinary jobs such as retail or cafe work and meet fans at events.[1]

Dokumo shape street fashion; the aomoji-kei look was launched by several of them in Harajuku.[1] Kyary Pamyu Pamyu is cited as a dokumo who rose through the magazine KERA, and others have moved into entertainment.[1][2] Dokumo-led makeup books are popular in bookstores.[1] Popteen's reader-model system is closely tied to gyaru fashion.[3]

timeline.event: Popteen launches; later known for reader models.[3]
